{{Short description|American mathematician (1939–2017)}}
'''Joyce Rogers McLaughlin''' (8 October 1939 – 23 October 2017)<ref>[https://sinews.siam.org/Details-Page/obituary-joyce-r-mclaughlin-6 Obituary: Joyce R. McLaughlin]</ref> was an American mathematician, the Ford Foundation Professor of Mathematics at [[Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute]].<ref name="skl"/> Her research interests were primarily in [[applied mathematics]], and in particular in [[inverse problem]]s.

==Academic career==
McLaughlin did her undergraduate studies at [[Kansas State University]]. After earning a master's degree from the [[University of Maryland]], she moved to the [[University of California, Riverside]] for her doctoral studies, earning a Ph.D. in 1968 under the supervision of Joaquin Basilio Diaz.<ref name="skl">[http://www.siam.org/prizes/2004_luncheon.php 2004 AWM-SIAM Sonia Kovalevsky Lecturer: Joyce R. McLaughlin], [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]], retrieved 2013-02-07.</ref><ref>{{mathgenealogy|name=Joyce Rogers McLaughlin|id=19536}}</ref> She joined the Rensselaer faculty in 1978.<ref name="skl"/>

She was chair of the board of trustees of the [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]] from 1996 to 1998.<ref name="skl"/>

==Awards and honors==
McLaughlin was an invited lecturer at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in 1994.
She was chosen by the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]] and the [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]] as the [[AWM-SIAM Sonia Kovalevsky Lecturer]] in 2004.<ref name="skl"/>

She became a fellow of the [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]] in 2009<ref>[http://fellows.siam.org/index.php?sort=year&value=2009 SIAM Fellows class of 2009], retrieved 2013-02-07.</ref> and a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]] in 2013 in the inaugural class.<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2013-02-06.</ref>
